hook.text: Touch a metal spoon in hot soup and the handle heats up—that's conduction, energy passing atom to atom.

buildup.text: In conduction, vibrating atoms bump into neighbors—energy flows through direct contact without any bulk motion.

discovery.text: Metals conduct heat well because free electrons carry energy quickly—that's also why they feel cold to the touch.

twist.text: Wood and plastic are poor conductors—trapped air pockets act as insulators, slowing energy transfer.

climax.text: Diamond conducts heat five times better than copper—its rigid crystal lattice transmits vibrations incredibly fast.

punchline.text: Atom bumps atom—and heat walks through solid matter.

quiz.question: Why are metals good heat conductors?
options: They have free electrons to carry energy
